pre_reveal_copy.headline: Crew reveal: June 9
pre_reveal_copy.subhead: NASA names the Artemis III astronauts on Tuesday at Johnson Space Center.
pre_reveal_copy.candidates_disclaimer: These are community-speculated candidates based on public information. Official crew announcement pending.

crew.name: Randy Bresnik
crew.short_bio: Marine Colonel and test pilot. Former commander of ISS Expedition 53.
bio_paragraphs: Randy Bresnik is a retired U.S. Marine Corps Colonel and a NASA astronaut selected in 2004. He flew on STS-129 in 2009 and commanded Expedition 53 on the International Space Station in 2017, logging four spacewalks.
His test pilot background and prior command experience put him on the manual loop for Artemis III's docking architecture — the riskiest unproven element of the mission.
career_highlights: U.S. Naval Test Pilot School graduate

crew.name: Luca Parmitano
crew.short_bio: Italian Air Force Colonel and ESA astronaut. First European on a crewed Artemis mission.
bio_paragraphs: Luca Parmitano is an Italian Air Force Colonel and ESA astronaut from the 2009 class. He flew Expedition 36/37 in 2013 — including the near-drowning spacewalk that reshaped NASA's EVA suit water-leak protocols — and commanded Expedition 61 in 2019.
His selection as Artemis III pilot is the first time a European astronaut has been assigned to a crewed Artemis mission, and is a significant moment for ESA's role in the program.
career_highlights: First European to command the ISS for ESA

crew.name: Frank Rubio
crew.short_bio: Army medical doctor and NASA astronaut. Holds the U.S. single-spaceflight record at 371 days.
bio_paragraphs: Frank Rubio is a U.S. Army Lieutenant Colonel and family physician selected as a NASA astronaut in 2017. His first spaceflight aboard Soyuz MS-22 was extended after a coolant leak on the original return vehicle, leaving him on the ISS for 371 days — the U.S. record for a single spaceflight.
On Artemis III, his medical background and operational endurance make him a known quantity for mission planners working a long-duration docking rehearsal in low Earth orbit.
career_highlights: U.S. record for longest single spaceflight (371 days, 2022–2023)
Black Hawk helicopter pilot, Army Special Operations
Family medicine and aerospace medicine board-certified

crew.name: Andre Douglas
crew.short_bio: Coast Guard officer and engineer, 2021 NASA astronaut class. First spaceflight.
bio_paragraphs: Andre Douglas is a U.S. Coast Guard officer and engineer selected in NASA's 2021 astronaut class — the first class chosen after Artemis was the program of record. His background includes work as a senior staff member at Johns Hopkins Applied Physics Laboratory on lunar surface systems.
Artemis III will be his first spaceflight.
career_highlights: Johns Hopkins Applied Physics Laboratory (lunar surface systems)
PhD, Systems Engineering, University of Michigan
